name: partner_mem_of_stdColDatum
summary: Average translates of p over the compact group GL_n(O), weighted by values of Ψ: the average lies in P and equals a positive multiple of Ψ, because Ψ is invariant under small translations and transforms by χ under GL_b(O).

steps.claim: Ψ is uniformly locally constant on integral translates: there is c with Ψ(y + ϖ^c z) = Ψ(y) for all integral z (hc), because ϖ is topologically nilpotent and the fibres of Ψ are open, uniformly over the compact set of integral matrices; and GL_n(O) is a compact space (`isCompact_intGL`).
steps.lean:
obtain ⟨⟨c, hc⟩, _⟩ := ((V.unif_nilpotent.smul_const (.id _)).eventually
    (ContinuousMap.eventually_mapsTo isCompact_O.matrix
    ((isLocallyConstant_curry (Q.mem_matchingPairs hχ hΨ).1.2 (· + ·) (-· + ·)).isOpen_fiber Ψ)
    (by simp_intro _))).exists, (isCompact_intGL (n := n) V.isCompact_O).compactSpace

steps.claim: Let d = ϖ^{−c}·(1 − x(s − ϖ^c s)) ∈ GL_n(F) (invertible: det(1 − x(1 − ϖ^c)s) = det(1 − (1 − ϖ^c)s x) = ϖ^{c·|b|}·…, using s x = 1 and Sylvester's identity).
steps.lean:
let d : GL n F := V.ϖ⁻¹ ^ c • .mk'' (1 - x * (s - V.ϖ ^ c • s))
    (by simp [↓det_one_sub_mul_comm x, *])

steps.claim: The function (k, y) ↦ p(d·k·y) is locally constant on GL_n(O) × (n × b matrices) (`schwartzBruhat.isLocallyConstant_curry`, p being Schwartz–Bruhat by hS).
steps.lean: have L := isLocallyConstant_curry (Γ := intGL n O) (hS hp) (d.1 * ·.1.1 * ·) (·.1.2 * d.2 * ·)

steps.claim: It suffices to show that N·Ψ ∈ P for N = ∫_{GL_n(O)} |p(d k x)| dk: this integral is positive (a continuous non-negative function on a compact group, non-zero at k = 1 where p(dx) = r(x)·stdColDatum(χ, s)(dx) ≠ 0 by h₁).

N·Ψ is the integral over k ∈ GL_n(O) of the functions Ψ(k₂x)·p(d k ·) (k₂ the second component of the point of GL_n(O)), each of which lies in P (hP and scalars), and the integral of a locally constant family in P over a compact group lies in P (`integral_mem_of_isLocallyConstant`); it remains to identify the two functions pointwise at each y.
steps.lean:
convert ← integral_mem_of_isLocallyConstant .haar (L.comp (norm ∘ · • Ψ)) fun k ↦
    (funext fun y ↦ ?_).subst (P.smul_mem (Ψ (k.1.2 * x)) (hP (d * k) _ hp))

steps.claim: Either Ψ(y) = 0 or y = firstCols(e, l) for some l ∈ GL_n(O) (support of a partner, Q); and x = firstCols(e, j) for some j ∈ GL_n(O), x being primitive (integral with integral left inverse s, `IsValuationPair.exists_firstCols_iff`).
steps.lean:
obtain ⟨_ | ⟨l, c, ⟨⟩⟩, j, a, ⟨⟩⟩ := not_or_of_imp (Q.2 ‹_›),
    (valPair.exists_firstCols_iff e).2 ⟨hx, by tauto⟩

steps.claim: In the case y = firstCols(e, l): substitute k ↦ k·(j⁻¹l) in the Haar integral over GL_n(O) (right invariance).
steps.lean: simp_all; rw [← integral_mul_right_eq_self _ ⟨_, div_mem a c⟩]

steps.claim: Rewrite the columns of products (`mul_firstCols`) and move the scalar into the integral.
Insert p = r·stdColDatum(χ, s) (H) and split on whether the matrix s·(…) is integral (i) with unit determinant (v); where it is, |χ| = 1 on the unit (`TameLocalChar.norm_eq_one`).
steps.lean: simp [H, invOnUnits]; split_ifs with i v <;> simp [hχ.norm_eq_one, *]

steps.claim: In that case s·(…) is a primitive square matrix, so it is an element g of GL_b(O) (`isPrimitiveMatrix_iff_isIntegralUnit_det`, `isPrimitiveMatrix_iff`).

By the transformation of a partner under right multiplication by g ∈ GL_b(O) (`IsPartner.right_mul`) and the local constancy hc (the difference is ϖ^c times an integral matrix), Ψ at the translated matrix equals Ψ(y), with the character factors cancelling.
steps.lean:
erw [← Q.right_mul _ m, ← congrFun (hc (k.2.isIntMatrix_inv.mul (i.sub (hx.mul m.isIntMatrix)))),
    (_ : V.ϖ ^ c • _ + _ = y)]; grind [hχ.norm_eq_one v, norm_zero]

steps.claim: The matrix identity behind step 11, ϖ^c·(…) + (…) = y, from the definition of d and s x = 1.
